clue.text: It is thrown in the arena to ' start the debate

definitions.text: It is thrown in the arena

indicators.note: only the start of the verb is wanted, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to debate a matter is to discuss it

explanation.surface: An athlete opens a forum argument by hurling something across the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' asks for the beginning of DISCUSS, the verb for 'debate', so drop its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy disc hurled by field athletes in a stadium is the object thrown in that event.

clue.text: Needs five changes' with one's back to the wall

definitions.text: with one's back to the wall

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cornered must make five adjustments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges NEEDS FIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cornered and fighting off attack is on the guard, protecting themselves.

clue.text: Unequally sided, with a learner in the scene

indicators.note: in says these letters are placed inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: A trainee driver appears in a lopsided scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and L inside SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle whose three sides all differ in length is scalene.

clue.text: Stuffs up gun-cases ?

parts.note: holsters are cases for carrying pistols

explanation.surface: Someone packs guns away in their cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffs' means pads with stuffing, as a furniture maker does to chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A furniture maker pads chairs with filling and covers them in fabric.

clue.text: Physicist makes a number go back by road maybe

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number

indicators.note: go back says the word go is written backwards
maybe says the letters of road may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A scientist arrives at a figure by retracing a road journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GO into OG; 'maybe' rearranges ROAD into ADRO. 'a number' fits the surface: Avogadro's number is the famous constant in chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Avogadro was the Italian scientist whose constant gives the number of particles in a mole.

clue.text: Evil in high places' under such rule ?.

definitions.text: Evil in high places' under such rule ?.

parts.note: vice is wickedness
regal means royal, belonging to those in high places

explanation.surface: Wickedness reaches the top under a certain kind of government.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a viceroy's rule stands in for the royal one, and its corruption is evil in high places.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a viceroy, who rules as the monarch's deputy in a colony.

clue.text: One poet about right for another

indicators.note: about says the first poet's name is wrapped round the other letter

parts.note: John Gay wrote The Beggar's Opera

explanation.surface: One poet's work is judged fitter than a rival's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts GAY round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray, author of the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, is a second poet.

clue.text: Like an aerial put up to cut off in a raid

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means written from bottom to top
in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: An antenna is erected to be severed during an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LOP inside RAID to give RALOPID; 'put up' turns it round to read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A common radio antenna has two poles, two rods fed at the centre.

clue.text: From nowhere maybe he has got something

indicators.note: maybe says the letters are rearranged once the other word is taken away

explanation.surface: A man from nowhere turns out to have something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From ... maybe' takes the letters H and E from NOWHERE and rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: One who possesses an item is its proprietor.

clue.text: Disagreeable ingredient of humble pie ?.

parts.note: eating humble pie has an American twin phrase naming a black bird as the unpleasant dish

explanation.surface: Something nasty has gone into a humbling pie.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'eat crow', the American idiom, is to eat humble pie, admitting one was wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The black bird is what one eats in the American idiom for humbling oneself.

clue.text: Lightweight in knock-down surprise

explanation.surface: A small boxer lands a surprise knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: A featherweight is a light boxing class; 'you could have knocked me down with a feather' is said of great surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the bird's plume: a featherweight boxer, and the idiom of being knocked down with a feather in astonishment.

clue.text: Contraction on aid given to climbers

parts.note: a cramp is a painful contraction of a muscle

explanation.surface: A climber's muscle seizes up while help is handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiked metal frame fixed to a boot is gear that helps mountaineers grip ice.

clue.text: Craft used in a timely : rescue ?

definitions.text: Craft used in a timely : rescue ?

parts.words: Craft used in a timely : rescue ?
parts.note: the proverb 'a stitch in time saves nine' makes sewing the skill behind a timely rescue

explanation.surface: Some vessel is put to use in a well-timed rescue at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat; it is a skill, sewing, which the proverb 'a stitch in time saves nine' credits with a timely save.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing and embroidery are the handicraft in which stitches are made.

clue.text: A slight bend in the bar

explanation.surface: A small curve appears in the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: In written music a curved line over notes in a bar, telling the player to join them smoothly, has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: An insult is a slight; in music the curved mark joining notes is a slur.

clue.text: Is this agent hidden ?

parts.note: a secret agent working in disguise is hidden

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a spy is concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy working under a false identity operates in secret.

clue.text: Plenty one altered unsuitably

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: altered says the letters of the word plenty are changed in order

explanation.surface: A large amount, once changed, ends up inappropriately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges PLENTY into NEPTLY, after I for 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in an inappropriate or clumsy way is doing it unsuitably.

clue.text: Punitive detective measure.?

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, the London police detective headquarters
the stick stands for punishment, as in carrot and stick

explanation.surface: A detective takes harsh measures.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police; 'the stick' means punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard used for judging something, originally a rod a yard long, is a gauge.

clue.text: Snare that ruined Mother ?

parts.note: gin is called 'mother's ruin', so a snare named after the spirit that ruined Mother

explanation.surface: A trap brought about Mother's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin is known as 'mother's ruin', and a gin is also an old word for a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-jawed trap for catching animals is the snare of this name.

clue.text: Asked out by letter, settling time later

parts.note: sending by letter is sending by post
someone asked out has been dated

explanation.surface: Someone asked out in writing agrees on a later time.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque marked with a future date has its settlement fixed for a later time.

clue.text: Salesman in Rome turns out to be *Augustus ?

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other
out says the letters of Rome are put out of order
turns says the salesman's word is reversed

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A travelling seller in the Italian capital is revealed as the first Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes REP into PER; 'out' scrambles ROME into EMOR; 'in' puts PER inside, between EM and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus was the first ruler of the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Master Pirrip and Miss Woodhouse, meet in — the afternoon

parts.note: Pip Pirrip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations
Emma Woodhouse is Jane Austen's heroine

explanation.surface: Two literary characters meet one afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip emma is old military signallers' speech for PM, the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old phonetic alphabet the letters for PM spell out a term for after noon.

clue.text: Old doctors were such stickers

explanation.surface: Doctors of old were the clinging kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Leech was an old word for a physician, and the bloodsucking worms that cling to skin are also leeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicians were once called by the worm's name, and the bloodsucking worms cling fast to their hosts.

clue.text: Moves on quickly to confound the sleuths

indicators.note: to confound is to mix up, so the letters of sleuths are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A suspect hurries away to baffle detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to confound' rearranges SLEUTHS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bustle someone along briskly is to hurry them, which is to move them on fast.

clue.text: Sort of 'chest used for the bottom drawer

definitions.text: Sort of 'chest used for the bottom drawer

parts.words: Sort of 'chest used for the bottom drawer
parts.note: in Britain a bride's store of linen is her bottom drawer; in America it is kept in a chest named for her expectations

explanation.surface: A kind of chest stores things in its lowest drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bottom drawer' is a British term for linen saved up for marriage; the American equivalent is a hope chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau chest, saved for marriage, takes this word for expectation as its name.

clue.text: Pledges with wines

explanation.surface: Someone pawns things along with bottles of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: To hock is to pawn; hock is also British for German white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawning an item is pledging it; Rhine whites are known in Britain by the name.

clue.text: Large fitting is traced somehow and -sent: away

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a large fitting in clothes

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of is traced are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: An oversized fixture is tracked down and sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges IS TRACED into TRACISED after OS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be banished or excluded from society is to be sent away.

clue.text: Got up, say, in ranks

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken, sounding like another

parts.note: to get up from bed is to rise, past tense rose

explanation.surface: Soldiers stood up in their ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means ROSE (got up) is pronounced like the word for lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of people or seats standing side by side are rows.

clue.text: Dentistry examination?

parts.note: a dentist examines the mouth, and a spoken test is also so named

explanation.surface: A trip to the dentist for a check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: A spoken test is an oral, and a dentist's check-up concerns the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the mouth, and also a spoken exam, both senses fit.

clue.text: French town, reached by. river and rail first class

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
BR is British Rail
A1 means first class, written AI

explanation.surface: A traveller reaches a French town by river and first-class train.
explanation.walkthrough: BR was British Rail, the old national railway; A1 (written AI) means first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambrai is a town in northern France, known for a First World War battle.

clue.text: A ripple on the surface of: 29, perhaps

definitions.text: A ripple on the surface of: 29, perhaps

parts.words: A ripple on the surface of: 29, perhaps
parts.note: 29 is a ballet with a lake in its title, and a small ripple on a lake is a little wave

explanation.surface: A small disturbance spreads across the water of a famous ballet's setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 across names a lake, so a ripple on it is a small wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wave is a ripple on water.

clue.text: .Where a ballerina takes to water-wings ?

parts.note: a dancer becomes a winged water bird in the famous Tchaikovsky ballet

explanation.surface: A dancer learns to swim using inflatable armbands.
explanation.walkthrough: Water-wings suggest swimming aids; here they are the wings of a water bird, which the ballerina plays in Tchaikovsky's ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's ballet has dancers playing swans on a lake.

clue.text: Wiped out by the turbulent Red Sea

indicators.note: turbulent waters are churned, so the letters of Red Sea are stirred up

explanation.surface: Pharaoh's army was destroyed by the stormy Red Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges RED SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something removed completely, like writing rubbed off, has been wiped out.
